item.title: Markets Challenge Warsh’s Approach to Taming Inflation
item.description: Kevin M. Warsh has made controlling inflation the top priority of his tenure as Federal Reserve chairman. But his hesitancy to embrace the possibility of higher borrowing costs has sparked a backlash.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Traders on the floor of the New York Stock Exchange as a screen broadcasts a news conference by Federal Reserve Chairman Kevin Warsh on Wednesday.

item.title: U.S. Economic Growth Slowed in the Second Quarter
item.description: Gross domestic product expanded at a 1.5 percent annual rate over the past three months, as war in the Middle East shook energy prices and supply chains.
item.dc:creator: Talmon Joseph Smith

item.title: Fed’s Preferred Inflation Gauge Eased During Pause in Iran War
item.description: Price pressures eased during a brief reprieve in the war with Iran, but the resumption of fighting suggests that inflation risks are still prevalent.
item.dc:creator: Colby Smith
item.media:description: Ships transiting through the Gulf of Oman on Saturday. After a brief truce, fresh fighting in the region this month could cause U.S. inflation to rise again.

item.title: A ‘Credibility Shock’ Looms Over the Fed
item.description: Bonds sold off sharply after the Federal Reserve’s latest rate decision, signaling growing turmoil between the markets and the central bank.
item.dc:creator: Andrew Ross Sorkin, Bernhard Warner, Sarah Kessler, Michael J. de la Merced, Niko Gallogly, Brian O’Keefe, Sri Muppidi and Ian Mount
item.media:description: The markets have reacted strongly to the news conference given by Kevin Warsh, the Fed chairman.

item.title: Poland’s Leader Says Russian Missile May Have Struck Its Territory During Ukraine Attack

item.title: Russia Strikes Ukraine With Missiles and Drones, Killing at Least 8
item.description: President Volodymyr Zelensky of Ukraine said that a family of five had been killed at home in the latest in a series of large-scale aerial assaults by Moscow.

item.title: As China’s A.I. Gets Stronger, It Poses New Risks to Beijing

item.media:credit: Pool photo by Ng Han Guan
item.media:description: The Chinese leader Xi Jinping opening the World A.I. Conference in Shanghai, China, in July. Even as China supports openness in A.I., it needs to “constantly refine measures to forestall loss of control,” he said.

item.title: A.I. Data Centers in Space? A System to Cool Chips Could Help.
item.description: Researchers at Caltech and Sophia Space, a start-up, have developed a technology using solar power to prevent computer equipment from overheating in orbit.
item.dc:creator: Ivan Penn
item.media:description: Small solar arrays, like those on the International Space Station, are already used in space, but A.I. data centers would require substantially more equipment for electricity generation.
